## board-read-marks: a role's Board read marks are the posts it was shown in full

- `local` (Ops #710; message-audit follow-up R6c, the owner picked "Both"; plan approved in Ops lead). Hypothesis H-R6c (`~/kept-from-tmp/2026-10-31/message-audit-gaps/GAPS.md`): `board read` without an id marked every open post read though it shows only titles (at most 20), and a turn note's seen-mark covered the posts it left out ("… and N more"), so later notes never showed them; the Roles page and order follow-up overstated what each role read. Marking only what is shown in full should make read marks equal the posts shown, with no post lost or repeated; wrong if notes repeat posts or the left-out posts never appear.
- `server/board-tool.ts`: `board read` without an id returns the list and marks nothing; `board read <id>` still marks that post (`RoleBoard.markRead`, unchanged).
- `server/role-board.ts` `boardNote`: the mark's `open` holds the posts seen before plus the ones this note shows, not every fresh one. `BoardMark` gets an optional `later` (the posts the note left out): the next note shows them in full (orders first, then by seq) and `turnNote` marks them then. `open` alone isn't enough: the left-out posts are already at or below `upTo`, so they would be hidden for good. A left-out post that closes before it is shown isn't shown as ended; one the chat gets directly counts as seen. `boardMarkOf` reads `later` back (absent or malformed: none), so older marks work as before.
- Checks: `tests/unit/role-board.test.ts`: with 25 open posts the list makes 0 reads and `board read <id>` 1; the first note shows and marks 20 ("… and 5 more"), the next the other 5, a third is empty, and news older than 3 days that a first turn skipped stays unshown; a left-out post closed, or got directly, before the next note isn't shown there or as ended; the existing tool test now expects the list to mark nothing. On the old code these 4 fail; on the new code all 40 pass.
- Unchanged: routing, order delivery, acks and closes.
- Undo: revert this commit and `pi-web-deploy` it. The old code reads a mark with `later` as a plain mark (it ignores the field), so the left-out posts go back to being skipped; nothing repeats.
